data.situation:
On Saturday, 29 May, Maya returned to the centre for her 9.30 appointment. Beyond the meeting table, two name cards stood outside the service room. One introduced the visiting medical practitioner; the other introduced a therapist working in a different part of the room. Maya had booked a conversation, not a massage, and checked her name against the appointment card. Inside, the practitioner placed a leaflet on the desk. It described support for people living with a long-term disorder and listed questions they could bring to an appointment. Maya asked who would deal with a question about an existing medical record. The practitioner pointed to the first card. Through the partly open door, someone was quietly arranging clean towels on a chair. SERVICE ROOM — SATURDAY, 29 MAY
Medical practitioner: booked consultations at the desk nearest the door.
Therapist: separate appointments beside the screened area. The service list includes massage.
Please check the name on your appointment card before entering. If you have brought a letter or an existing medical record, tell the person handling your appointment.

readingBlocks.en: On Saturday, 29 May, Maya returned to the centre for her 9.30 appointment. Beyond the meeting table, two name cards stood outside the service room. One introduced the visiting medical practitioner; the other introduced a therapist working in a different part of the room. Maya had booked a conversation, not a massage, and checked her name against the appointment card. Inside, the practitioner placed a leaflet on the desk. It described support for people living with a long-term disorder and listed questions they could bring to an appointment. Maya asked who would deal with a question about an existing medical record. The practitioner pointed to the first card. Through the partly open door, someone was quietly arranging clean towels on a chair.
readingBlocks.zh: 5月29日周六，玛雅又来到中心，赴上午九点半的预约。会议桌再往里，服务室门外立着两张姓名卡。一张介绍来访的医师，另一张介绍在房间另一处工作的治疗师。玛雅预约的是一次咨询，不是按摩；她对照预约卡确认了自己的名字。进门后，医师把一份传单放在桌上。传单介绍为长期患有某种疾病的人提供的支持，并列出了他们可以带到预约中询问的问题。玛雅问，关于已有病历的问题该由谁处理。医师指了指第一张卡。透过半开的门，她看见有人正把干净毛巾轻轻摆在椅子上。

readingBlocks.en:
SERVICE ROOM — SATURDAY, 29 MAY
Medical practitioner: booked consultations at the desk nearest the door.
Therapist: separate appointments beside the screened area. The service list includes massage.
Please check the name on your appointment card before entering. If you have brought a letter or an existing medical record, tell the person handling your appointment.
readingBlocks.zh:
服务室——5月29日周六
医师：在靠门的桌旁接待已预约的咨询。
治疗师：在屏风旁另行接待预约，服务项目包括按摩。
进门前请核对预约卡上的姓名。如果带来了信件或已有病历，请告诉接待你这次预约的人员。

glossary.note: medical practitioner 明确医疗角色；单独 practitioner 也可指其他领域的实践者。
glossary.example: One introduced the visiting medical practitioner; the other introduced a therapist working in a different part of the room.
glossary.exampleZh: 一张介绍来访的医师，另一张介绍在房间另一处工作的治疗师。

externalEvidence.definition: someone who practices a learned profession

glossary.zh: 提供治疗服务的治疗师
glossary.note: therapist 是治疗领域的泛称；仅凭这个词不能断定是医师、理疗师或心理治疗师。
glossary.example: One introduced the visiting medical practitioner; the other introduced a therapist working in a different part of the room.
glossary.exampleZh: 一张介绍来访的医师，另一张介绍在房间另一处工作的治疗师。

externalEvidence.definition: a person skilled in a particular type of therapy

glossary.zh: 身体功能出现问题的疾病或障碍
glossary.note: a long-term disorder 表示长期的疾病或功能障碍；这里的 disorder 用于身体状况。
glossary.example: It described support for people living with a long-term disorder and listed questions they could bring to an appointment.
glossary.exampleZh: 传单介绍为长期患有某种疾病的人提供的支持，并列出了他们可在预约时询问的问题。

externalEvidence.definition: a physical condition in which there is a disturbance of normal functioning

glossary.note: a massage 是一次按摩；have a massage 表示接受按摩。
glossary.example: Maya had booked a conversation, not a massage, and checked her name against the appointment card.
glossary.exampleZh: 玛雅预约的是咨询，不是按摩；她对照预约卡确认了自己的名字。
